business_problem: Unimed Grande Florianopolis needed to replace fragmented spreadsheets and departmental systems so it could standardize healthcare data, run predictive analysis, monitor operations in real time, and reduce fraud and manual reporting work.
solution_summary: Unimed Grande Florianopolis adopted Oracle Analytics Cloud as its enterprise analytics layer after evaluating architecture, integration, and cost options through a proof of concept. Oracle Analytics Cloud consolidates operational and hospital data that had been spread across spreadsheets and disconnected systems, then delivers dashboards for mobile access and digital displays. The platform's AI and machine learning features are used to support predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and healthcare-specific analysis across preventive medicine, bed provisioning, operational indicators, and fraud detection. Because the analytics environment is fed from standardized data instead of manual spreadsheet work, the health cooperative can track patient flows and treatment-management needs more reliably while reducing time spent preparing monthly reports. The result is a single analytics environment that supports cost savings, compliance, and data-driven patient and operations management.

solution_components.name: Oracle Analytics Cloud
solution_components.role: Centralizes healthcare data analysis, predictive models, dashboards, and anomaly detection for operations and patient management.

data_flow: Hospital and business data from previously disconnected spreadsheets and departmental systems is consolidated into Oracle Analytics Cloud, where dashboards, predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting are used by managers and care teams for operational and patient-management decisions.
business_outcome: Unimed Grande Florianopolis reduced healthcare costs, saved manual reporting time, improved fraud detection, and gained a more reliable analytics culture for patient management and operational decision-making.
